author: agent
text: Flag ownership is a TUPLE of commands, not one command. It was one owner per flag for a year, and `memway viz --force` - a flag printed in viz's own usage line - was rejected with "applies to 'pull' only" because pull claimed --force first. The deeper reason nothing caught it: the usage text lives in this module's docstring and the flag table lived inside main(), and no test compared them. VALUE_FLAGS/BOOL_FLAGS are now module-level SO THEY CAN BE READ BY A TEST; tests/test_cli_usage.py parses the flags back out of the shipped usage text (12 flags across 7 commands, parsed not hand-listed) and requires each to be receivable by the command it is printed under. Do not re-inline these tables into main(). Fixed 0.53.3, 2026-08-16.

author: cli
text: Re-read after 0.55.2. The flag-ownership paragraph above is untouched and still exact: VALUE_FLAGS/BOOL_FLAGS remain module-level, the usage text is still parsed back out in tests/test_cli_usage.py, and nothing was re-inlined. The hash moved because dispatch gained a branch: an unrecognised command used to fall into the same 'print the whole docstring' path as a bare invocation, so 'memway freshness .' scrolled the entire quickstart past without ever naming the word it did not recognise. Unknown commands now get one stderr line plus a difflib suggestion. NOTE THE TRAP THAT CAUGHT ME: --help is not in COMMANDS and had been relying on that shared fallthrough, so splitting the branch broke it in four existing tests. --help/-h/help are named explicitly now. Same lesson as the flag table - the usage surface and the dispatch table are two descriptions of one thing, and only tests that read both catch the gap.
